content.title: Contact-Triggered Medium Toggle | Registered Progress to a Real Finished Object
content.summary: Lock one workspace and object, then make every visible tool contact toggle the registered region between photoreal reality and one distinct illustrated medium. Preserve anchors while each transition advances an irreversible construction state, and end by returning to the complete real object.

quick_start.input_format: locked workspace and object + visible contact tool + at least two real/illustrated round trips + fixed registration anchors + one irreversible progress stage after each toggle + completed photoreal object return
quick_start.recommended_input: On a locked watchmaker bench, a white chalk stylus toggles one brass clock module between photoreal metal and cobalt technical line art. Each contact adds a base plate, gear train, spring, hands, or crystal while three fixed screws preserve registration; the final contact restores the complete real clock and begins one steady tick.
required_anchors: Establish one bounded workspace, one primary object and one visible contact tool in reality.
Toggle medium only at visible tool contact and preserve object registration across the boundary.
Advance one irreversible build or preparation state after every toggle without resetting earlier progress.
Return to photoreal reality with the completed object and original anchors visible.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Lock one workspace and object, then make every visible tool contact toggle the registered region between photoreal reality and one distinct illustrated medium. Preserve anchors while each transition advances an irreversible construction state, and end by returning to the complete real object.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Lock one bounded workspace, one primary object and one visible contact tool. Every time the tool touches the object or its immediate support, toggle the registered region between photoreal action and a materially distinct illustrated medium. Preserve object orientation, support geometry and surrounding anchors across each toggle, while advancing one irreversible construction or preparation state after every transition. End by returning to photoreal reality with the completed object and all accumulated evidence visible. The reusable mechanism is attributable contact, registered medium toggle, irreversible progress, anchor continuity and real finished payoff—not the source hand, blue stylus, bread, egg, pan, French toast, berries, syrup, black-yellow drawing style, exact camera, timing, creator identity or model labels.

invariants.rule: Establish one bounded workspace, one primary object and one visible contact tool in reality.
invariants.purpose: Defines the registered region and causal trigger.
invariants.ablation_failure: An unseen trigger makes the medium switch arbitrary.

invariants.rule: Toggle medium only at visible tool contact and preserve object registration across the boundary.
invariants.purpose: Makes every transformation attributable and comparable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Cuts between unrelated layouts lose contact causality.

invariants.rule: Alternate between photoreal and one clearly different illustrated medium at least twice.
invariants.purpose: Proves a repeatable two-way system rather than a single effect.
invariants.ablation_failure: One-way conversion does not establish a toggle grammar.

invariants.rule: Advance one irreversible build or preparation state after every toggle without resetting earlier progress.
invariants.purpose: Turns medium change into narrative progress.
invariants.ablation_failure: Cosmetic switching alone is a filter demo.

invariants.rule: Return to photoreal reality with the completed object and original anchors visible.
invariants.purpose: Closes both medium and progress arcs.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending in illustration leaves real completion unproven.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source hand, light-blue stylus and exact contact positions
the source kitchen, plate, pan, bread, egg, French toast, berries, sugar and syrup
the source black-and-yellow illustration style, line density and drawing marks
the source camera positions, object orientation, transition timing and plating sequence
the source creator identity, GPT Image 2 and Seedance 2.0 labels, platform overlay, watermark and branding
